newsitem.title: ESTONIA: GOVERNMENT ENDS FIRST READING OF BUDGET.
newsitem.headline: GOVERNMENT ENDS FIRST READING OF BUDGET.

text.p: The government has completed the first reading of the 1998 budget, which foresees around a 10.3 percent rise in the total budget amount to 13.8 billion kroons, domestic news agency ETA said.
The budget includes for the first time revenue from import duties of 30 to 40 million kroons.
ETA quoted the government press service as saying that the cabinet late on Tuesday finished the first reading and that ministers have to make their written proposals later.
It said that the budget has no rise in the tax burden and that most additional revenue will come from excise duties on fuel of 2.66 billion kroons, 14 percent more than in 1997.
Excise duties are to be raised step-by-step to 2002 to reach EU levels, ETA said.
The state also plans to collect 13 percent more income tax or 2.55 billion kroons and 11 percent more VAT or 6.41 billion kroons.
Revenue from corporate income tax has been planned at a four percent rise to 1.144 billion kroons if it remains unchanged at 26 percent although there are proposals to cut it to 15 percent.
The government also wants to freeze administrative expenses at 1997 levels in the 1998 budget, ETA added.
